sentence: Not only does the treatise draw upon classical philosophy but it also engages with contemporary discourse
hint: Inversion after 'Not only': Not only + auxiliary + subject
explanation: 'Draw upon' significa usar como fuente. 'Engage with' significa interactuar intelectualmente. Conjunción correlativa con inversión.

sentence: Were one to pore over the archival records the discrepancies would become self-evident
hint: Formal conditional: Were + subject + to + base form
explanation: 'Pore over' significa estudiar detenidamente. 'Were one to' es un condicional muy formal con el 'one' impersonal.

sentence: The dissertation sets out to dismantle the prevailing orthodoxy on cognitive development
explanation: 'Set out to' significa tener la intención de o proponerse. Presente con sujeto singular: 'sets out'.

sentence: Never before had a single publication brought about such a paradigm shift in the field
explanation: 'Bring about' significa causar. 'Never before' provoca inversión con el pasado perfecto.

sentence: The critic took issue with the author's tendency to gloss over methodological limitations
explanation: 'Take issue with' significa estar en desacuerdo. 'Gloss over' significa tratar algo de forma superficial.

sentence: Only through sustained inquiry can scholars tease out the nuances of such complex phenomena
explanation: 'Tease out' significa extraer con cuidado. Es separable: 'tease the nuances out' también es correcto. 'Only through' provoca inversión.

sentence: It is essential that the peer reviewers not shy away from rigorous scrutiny
hint: Subjunctive: It is essential that + subject + base form
explanation: 'Shy away from' significa evitar. Modo subjuntivo después de 'it is essential that'.

sentence: The monograph builds on decades of empirical research to put forward a unified theory
explanation: 'Build on' significa usar como base. 'Put forward' significa proponer. Sujeto singular: 'builds'.

sentence: Under no circumstances should the findings be passed off as conclusive without replication
explanation: 'Pass off as' significa presentar algo de forma engañosa. La frase negativa provoca inversión con voz pasiva.

sentence: Had the theorist not zeroed in on the anomalous data the breakthrough would have remained elusive
explanation: 'Zero in on' significa enfocarse con precisión. Condicional invertida para un pasado irreal.

sentence: The validity of the argument hinges on a single contested premise
explanation: 'Hinge on' significa depender por completo de un único factor.

sentence: The ambiguous phrasing gave rise to conflicting interpretations
explanation: 'Give rise to' significa causar o dar lugar a algo.

sentence: Much of the controversy stems from methodological inconsistencies
explanation: 'Stem from' significa originarse o resultar de algo.

sentence: Subsequent findings bore out the theorist's original conjecture
explanation: 'Bear out' significa confirmar una afirmación. Es separable: 'bore the conjecture out' también es correcto.

sentence: The discrepancy calls into question the study's overall validity
explanation: 'Call into question' significa poner en duda algo.

sentence: The findings run counter to previous assumptions in the field
explanation: 'Run counter to' significa ir en contra de algo establecido.

sentence: Researchers must periodically take stock of the available evidence
hint: Subject + modal + adverb + phrasal verb + object
explanation: 'Take stock of' significa evaluar cuidadosamente una situación.

sentence: Sustained criticism gradually chipped away at public confidence
explanation: 'Chip away at' significa debilitar algo poco a poco.

sentence: The additional data lends credence to the original hypothesis
explanation: 'Lend credence to' significa dar credibilidad a algo.

sentence: Ethical concerns have increasingly come to the fore in recent debates
hint: Subject + present perfect + adverb + phrasal verb + place
explanation: 'Come to the fore' significa volverse prominente o importante.
